title: Databases: records, fields and filters
p: A database keeps records that share the same fields: books you are reading, feedback you collect, a list of contacts. Each field has a type, so a date stays a date and a rating stays a number of stars. For a database to try, open Reading list in this folder: twenty books, with a field of each type.

ul.li: Choose Database from the New menu of a folder. The database is a .sqlite file of its own in your documents folder.
In a page, type /data and choose Database to put one inside the page. Hover over it and choose Full screen to give it the whole window.

p: This page has one: a small database kept with the page, logging a week of reading. Edit it here, or give it the whole window.

ul.li: Edit a cell: click it and type, or press Enter. Tab and the arrow keys move between cells.
Add a record: click Add record at the top left, or the plus below the last row; right-click a row to insert one above or below it.
Open a record: click the expand control at the start of a row, or right-click it and choose Open record, to see and edit every field at once.
Add a field: click the plus control after the last column, name it and pick its type.
Change a field: click a column header and choose Edit field to rename it or change its type. Existing values are converted where they can be.

td.p: Typed values with their own formats: a number can show as a percentage, a currency with its symbol
Choose from options; each option has a color
A calendar picker, a tick box, stars
Links that open, and files kept with the database
An address or place, a code such as an ISBN
A value computed from other fields, such as {Price} * {Quantity}
Each cell is a page of its own: click an empty cell and choose New note, or point it to an existing note
Auto number, Date created, Last modified time

p: The tools at the top right filter, sort and group the records, choose which fields show, set the row height and color rows; Search records finds text in any cell. A column header's menu offers the same for that field: Filter by this field, Sort A to Z, Group by this field, or Hide field.

callout.p: Filters, sorts and groups change what you see, not the records. Clear them to see every record again.

ul.li: Select cells and copy them: they paste into a spreadsheet as rows and columns, or into another database.
Paste rows from a spreadsheet or a CSV file into a database to add them.
The … menu at the top right exports the database as CSV or copies it as a Markdown table.

p: A Note field links each record to a document in your library. Guide index in this folder lists these guides that way: its second field, Guide, is a Note field. Double-click a Guide cell to read that guide beside its record, and choose Open as a page at the top of the panel to give it the whole window. The fields after it say what you want to know about each guide: its folder, its type, the reading order, the minutes it takes, whether you have read it.

ul.li: Rename a document or move it to another folder, and its cell still finds it.
To link a document you already have, right-click a Note cell and choose Point to an existing note.

p: Keep your own documents the same way: a project's pages with their status, meeting notes by date, the articles you are drafting.

Every database is a plain SQLite file: its records sit in an SQL table, with the fields as columns and the values you see. Other tools, scripts and agents can read and change it without knowing Quiet.md; it picks up their changes the next time it reads the file.
